(a) the rate of economic growth is a decreasing function of the level of technology and an increasing function of the level and the rate of change of institutional development; (b) the rate of technological change is an increasing function of both the rate and the level of institutional development; and (c) the rate of institutional development is a function of the rate of economic and technological growth, the level and the rates of change of technology and institutions, and the level and the direction of institutional change.

the institutional framework, the socio-economic system, is a dynamic, self-organizing, self-regulating, and self-renewing mechanism which, by its very nature, is subject to the forces of growth.
the institutional structure is the most important determinant of the rate of growth of the economy, and that the institutional structure itself is the product of technological progress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
technological progress and institutional innovation are two complementary forces that have been responsible for the long-run growth of the economy.
the institutional framework, in its various manifestations, is a determinant of the expansionary potential and of the stability of an economy.
technological progress and institutional changes are the main driving forces of the economic development of a society, and they are closely interrelated.
